title_en: A Room With a View, Almost
description_ru: Диалог на стойке регистрации отеля: гость выясняет, почему забронированный номер оказался не тем, и договаривается о решении.
text:
Iris: Good evening, and welcome to the Hotel Marlowe. How may I help you?
Mr Lang: Good evening. I have a reservation in the name of Lang. I booked a double room with a sea view for four nights, and I paid in advance.
Iris: Let me check that for you. Lang, L-A-N-G. Yes, I can see your booking here. Could I have your passport, please?
Mr Lang: Of course. Here you are. I must say that I have been looking forward to this trip for months. My wife and I are celebrating our thirtieth anniversary.
Iris: Congratulations. That is wonderful news. Oh dear.
Mr Lang: Oh dear? I do not like the sound of that.

Iris: I am afraid there has been a slight misunderstanding. According to the system, the room that was reserved for you is on the second floor, and it faces the car park.
Mr Lang: The car park? But the confirmation email clearly said sea view. I have it on my phone, if you would like to see it.
Iris: There is no need, sir. I believe you. It seems that the website was updated last month, and some of the older bookings were not correctly transferred. I do apologise.
Mr Lang: I appreciate the apology, but I am not sure that it solves anything. What exactly can be done?
Iris: Let me see what we have available. Please bear with me for a moment.
Mr Lang: Take your time. Although, between you and me, my wife has been travelling for eleven hours, and I would not like to be the one to give her the news.

Iris: I have two options. The first is a room on the fifth floor with a partial sea view. You can see the water, but only if you lean slightly out of the window.
Mr Lang: Lean out of the window? That sounds like a recipe for an accident.
Iris: I admit it is not ideal. The second option is a suite on the top floor, which has a balcony and a full view of the bay. However, it was booked for tomorrow by another guest, so we could only offer it for the first two nights.
Mr Lang: And what happens on the third night?
Iris: You would be moved to a different room, which has also been confirmed with a sea view. The staff would transfer your luggage during the day, so you would not need to do anything.
Mr Lang: Hmm. Moving in the middle of an anniversary trip is not exactly romantic.

Iris: I understand completely, sir. Let me speak to the manager, because I think that an exception could be made. One moment.
Mr Lang: Please do. And if you could find a way to avoid the move, I would be very grateful.
Iris: Mr Dunmore says that the guest in the suite has been contacted, and that he agreed to a different room, as long as he receives a free breakfast. So the suite is yours for all four nights.
Mr Lang: That is excellent news. I must say, you have been remarkably helpful. Is there any extra charge?
Iris: None at all. In fact, the hotel would like to offer you a bottle of wine and a dinner for two in our restaurant, with our compliments.
Mr Lang: That is very generous. My wife will be delighted, though I should warn you that she is very particular about fish.

Iris: Then I will tell the chef. He was trained in Lisbon, and he says that his grilled sea bass has been praised by critics.
Mr Lang: Splendid. And what time is breakfast served?
Iris: From seven to ten on weekdays, and until eleven at weekends. You can also ask for it to be brought to your room, if you prefer.
Mr Lang: Room service sounds like heaven. By the way, is the wi-fi included? I have been told that some hotels in this area charge extra for it.
Iris: It is free throughout the building, and the password is on your key card. If there is any problem, just dial nine from the phone in your room.

Mr Lang: One more thing, and then I will let you go. Is it possible to book a table at a restaurant in the old town for Saturday? My wife read about a place that was supposed to be famous for its seafood.
Iris: I would be glad to do that. Do you remember the name?
Mr Lang: I think it was called The Anchor, or perhaps The Lantern. I really cannot recall. It was something nautical.
Iris: Both are good, but The Anchor is more famous, and it gets very crowded. If you give me a moment, I will call them now, and if there is a table, I will reserve it for eight o'clock.
Mr Lang: You are a lifesaver. I will go and fetch my wife from the lobby before she thinks I have run away.

Iris: Here is your key card, Mr Lang. The suite is number 501, and the lift is on your left. A porter will bring your bags in a few minutes.
Mr Lang: Thank you once again. I came here fearing the worst, and I am leaving with a better room than I paid for.
Iris: That is how it should be, sir. Please do not hesitate to call if there is anything else we can do.
Mr Lang: I certainly will. Good night, Iris, and thank you for turning a disaster into an anniversary present.
Iris: It was a pleasure. Enjoy your stay, and happy anniversary to you both.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Плавно переходите от «э» к «и»; это долгий скользящий звук, а не короткое «э».
Губы сильно округлены, как для «у»; нижняя губа не касается зубов.
Верхние зубы касаются нижней губы, голос включён; не заменяйте на «ф».
Начальные «p, t, k» произносите с лёгким выдохом, как будто дуете на ладонь.

questions.question: What was the problem with Mr Lang's room?
questions.answer: It faced the car park instead of the sea.

questions.question: Why did the hotel make a mistake?
questions.answer: The website was updated and some bookings were not transferred correctly.

questions.question: What did the hotel offer as compensation?
questions.answer: The top-floor suite, a bottle of wine and a dinner for two.
